extracted.intended_audience: Guardian journalists, editors and other GNM newsroom staff
extracted.subtask_description: The Guardian News & Media (GNM) Editorial Code of Practice and Guidance (2023) sets organisation-wide standards for reporting and publishing across print, online and social, including updated guidance for use of generative AI. It covers core standards (accuracy, privacy, discrimination, grief, right of reply), implicit newsworthiness criteria, and categories of material that should not be published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify facts before publication; Distinguish news from opinion; Use named sources where possible; Cite/credit other journalists' work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verification is required prior to publication. Be clear about what is fact versus commentary. Prefer named sources when available; where others' reporting is used, cite and credit that work. Avoid publishing unverified claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Default to privacy unless overriding public interest; Special protection for children, vulnerable people; Respect for grief and shock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume individuals' privacy should be respected unless a clear public interest justifies intrusion. Give special protection to children and other vulnerable people and be sensitive to those in grief or shock when deciding what to publish and how to approach them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid prejudicial reference to race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, disability; Reference only when genuinely relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include prejudicial or stereotyping references. Only mention protected characteristics when they are genuinely relevant to the story and add necessary context to avoid discriminatory framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intrusion into Grief
rubrics_metrics.description: Sensitivity in approach; Justified by public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach victims and bereaved people with particular sensitivity. Any intrusion into grief must be justified by a clear public interest and handled with care regarding timing, language and prominence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of Reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjects of allegations get opportunity to respond; Reply published with prominence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer those accused or criticised a fair opportunity to reply before or promptly after publication. When published, replies should appear with appropriate prominence and balance relative to the allegation.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI Guidance (generative AI use)
rubrics_metrics.description: Material created with generative AI raises bias, ownership, plagiarism, IP issues; Disclosure expected; Verification still required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose where material has been created or substantially assisted by generative AI. Treat AI-generated content as requiring the same fact-checking and verification as other material. Be mindful of bias, provenance, copyright and plagiarism risks when using AI tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public interest (implicit newsworthiness criterion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A legitimate public interest can justify overriding the default presumption of privacy. Assess and document why public interest applies, ensuring it is genuine and proportionate to any intrusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth and accuracy (implicit newsworthiness criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Truth and accuracy are central to newsworthiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure reporting is truthful and accurate; corroborate claims, correct errors promptly and transparently, and avoid speculation presented as fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuine relevance of identifying details
rubrics_metrics.description: Genuine relevance of identifying details — identify only when relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include identifying details about people only when they are genuinely relevant to the story. Avoid gratuitous naming or images that serve no informational purpose and may harm private individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity to victims
rubrics_metrics.description: Sensitivity to victims must inform reporting decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give extra care to language, imagery and timing when reporting on victims. Avoid re-traumatisation and gratuitous detail; balance public interest against harm to victims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source credibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and disclose the reliability of sources. Prefer named, verifiable sources; be cautious with anonymous or single-source allegations and seek corroboration where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-discrimination in framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Anti-discrimination in framing — avoid biased presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame stories to avoid perpetuating bias or prejudice. Consider impact on protected groups and ensure coverage does not reinforce stereotypes or marginalisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction of news from opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction of news from opinion must be maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly separate factual reporting from commentary or opinion pieces so readers can distinguish verified facts from interpretation or argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about methods and AI
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency about AI / methods — disclose use and methods where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about newsgathering methods, including the use of AI tools, and disclose material assistance or significant methodological choices that affect content credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not publish unverified claims
rubrics_metrics.description: What should not be published: Unverified claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid publishing allegations or claims that have not been verified. If reporting unverified claims for public interest reasons, clearly indicate their status and seek corroboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not publish privacy intrusions without public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: What should not be published: Privacy intrusions without public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not publish private information or intrusive material unless a clear and proportionate public interest justification exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not publish discriminatory framing
rubrics_metrics.description: What should not be published: Discriminatory framing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from publishing wording or presentations that discriminate, marginalise or stigmatise individuals or groups on protected characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not publish material from undisclosed payments
rubrics_metrics.description: What should not be published: Material from undisclosed payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject or explicitly disclose material that results from payments or commercial arrangements that are not transparent to readers; undisclosed paid-for content undermines editorial integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not publish subterfuge without justification
rubrics_metrics.description: What should not be published: Subterfuge without justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using deception or undercover methods unless strictly necessary and justified by strong public interest; document the rationale and obtain appropriate editorial/legal sign-off when subterfuge is used.
